source.filename: 2022-Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon.pdf

actuation: Electrical Joule heating (PWM-controlled AC for SMP, direct AC for SMA)
Pneumatic vacuum / air evacuation (below -90 kPa) and air injection
constitutive_assumptions: Euler-Bernoulli linear beam bending under a concentrated point load at the cantilever tip (P/delta = 3*n*E*I / L^3)
Linear elastic force-displacement relationship below 20 N force and 10 mm displacement
Isotropic linear elastic modulus for SMP below Tg (1350 MPa) and above Tg (4.5 MPa)
Isotropic linear elastic modulus for Ni-Ti SMA in martensite (28 GPa) and austenite (75-83 GPa) phases
Assumption of decoupled outer membrane deflection in the unjammed state below Tg (membrane deforms locally without engaging SMP)
Assumption of unified composite bending deformation between outer membrane and shape-memory core in the jammed state
control_variables: Applied displacement amplitude in Condition 1 (10 mm) and Condition 2 (2 mm)
Force threshold for linear stiffness calculation (below 20 N)
Vacuum pressure level during jamming (below -90 kPa)
Heating temperature setpoint for SMP (70 deg C) maintained via PWM control
Applied AC heating voltage (8 V AC for SMP, 3 V AC for SMA)
Dead weight magnitude for shape fixity test (2 kg)
Outer silicone membrane dimensions (outer diameter 34 mm, thickness 2 mm, length 100 mm) and material (ECOFLEX 00-30)
Granular jamming media type (coarse coffee grounds, 24 g for Prototype 1, 26 g for Prototype 2)
dependent_variables: Bending stiffness (N/mm, gradient of linear approximation of force-displacement)
Tip displacement (mm) under point loading and constant 2 kg load
Shape recovery time (s / min) and residual distance from initial position (mm)
Reaction force hysteresis and cyclic degradation over 10 reciprocating cycles
Self-weight supporting capability in horizontal cantilever configuration
Object gripping success across five distinct test items

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Shape-memory polymers exhibit a reversible elastic modulus change between glassy and rubbery states on the order of 100 to 1000 times across the glass transition temperature, enabling low-load deformation when heated and rigid shape fixity when cooled.
Granular jamming achieves rapid transitions between compliant fluid-like and rigid load-bearing solid-like states upon air evacuation on millisecond timescales.
By integrating a shape-memory material (SMP or SMA) with granular jamming within an elastomeric membrane, the variable-stiffness link achieves four distinct stiffness states.

For the SMP-based link (Prototype 1), vertical bending stiffness varied by approximately 33 times between the unjammed state above Tg and the jammed state below Tg, with granular jamming exerting a greater effect on stiffness change than SMP temperature modulation alone.

In contrast to conventional granular jamming manipulators that struggle to support their self-weight horizontally, both hybrid prototypes supported their own weight in an unjammed horizontal cantilever configuration.

In the unjammed state below Tg, measured stiffness (0.23 N/mm) was lower than Euler-Bernoulli beam calculations (0.56 N/mm) because the outer membrane deformed locally without deforming the SMP core, whereas under jamming the stiffness difference across Tg (0.68 N/mm) closely matched calculation (0.56 N/mm) due to coupled composite deformation.
Prototype 2 using four circular SMA wires recovered its initial shape in 0.24 times the duration required by Prototype 1 with SMP sheets.
Both prototype links sustained a constant 2 kg dead load at the cantilever tip for 1 hour without continuous creep after initial deflection, verifying rigid shape fixity.

Neither prototype achieved perfect shape recovery to the initial position, which was attributed to the small recovery force of thin SMP sheets and non-uniform distribution of coffee grounds in the membrane.

The links successfully conformed to and gripped diverse geometric objects (spanner, spring, pen, spray can cap, ballpoint pen) utilizing shape fixity prior to vacuum evacuation to expand contact area.

experimental_setup: Prototype 1 fabrication: Two polyurethane SMP sheets (MP4510, Tg = 45 deg C, 74 mm x 31 mm x 1.5 mm) with embedded nichrome heating wires (0.26 mm diameter, 5.2 ohm total resistance) stacked on a 3D-printed jig in cantilever configuration, encased in a silicone rubber membrane (ECOFLEX 00-30, outer diameter 34 mm, thickness 2 mm, length 100 mm) filled with 24 g of coarse coffee grounds, sealed with air filters and connected to a vacuum pump evacuating below -90 kPa. Joule heating maintained at 70 deg C via 8 V AC transformer and LabVIEW PWM control with surface thermocouple feedback.

Prototype 2 fabrication: Four straight Ni-Ti SMA wires (diameter 1.0 mm, circle diameter 30 mm, As = 60 deg C, 0.46 ohm total resistance) fixed into a 3D-printed jig with silicone plug and air filters, encased in an identical silicone membrane with 26 g coarse coffee grounds, powered directly with 3 V AC.

Stiffness test bench: Prototype link fixed horizontally in cantilever mode on an automated motorized stage (Sigma Koki SGSP26-50, translation speed 2 mm/s) applying point loads against a Kyowa LVS-2KA load cell under Condition 1 (monotonic 10 mm deflection, 5 trials) and Condition 2 (10 reciprocating cycles of 2 mm deflection at 20 Hz acquisition) along vertical and horizontal axes.

Shape fixity apparatus: Cantilever prototype loaded with a 2 kg dead weight at 50 mm position horizontally for 1 hour, with tip displacement recorded continuously using a Keyence IL-S100 / IL-1000 laser displacement sensor.

Gripping evaluation: Manual conformal wrapping around five test objects of varied shapes and masses (18 g spanner, 3 g spring, 20 g pen, 5 g spray can cap, 11 g ballpoint pen) followed by cooling/shape fixity and vacuum evacuation.
future_work: Optimize internal structures according to shape-memory material properties, including forming SMA wires into complex 3D shapes such as coils.
Optimize selection and formulation of SMP and SMA materials to tailor transition temperatures, hysteresis, and recovery strains to application requirements.
Optimize granular filler material and incorporate internal membrane partitions to prevent particle redistribution and ensure uniform distribution.
Implement closed-loop temperature control for SMA wires similar to the SMP control system.
Develop autonomous actuation/deformation mechanisms to eliminate reliance on manual shaping.
Integrate the deformable link onto a robotic arm and evaluate performance in realistic manipulation tasks.
Quantitatively evaluate gripping capacity through load-cell pull-off force testing.
independent_variables: Thermal state of shape-memory element (below Tg vs. above Tg at 70 deg C for SMP; low-temperature martensite vs. Joule-heated austenite for SMA)
Pneumatic pressure state of granular jamming mechanism (atmospheric unjammed vs. evacuated below -90 kPa jammed)
Loading direction relative to orthotropic SMP sheet orientation (vertical vs. horizontal)
Shape-memory material type and geometry (two stacked SMP sheets vs. four circular SMA wires)
Number of cyclic loading iterations (up to 10 cycles in Condition 2)
Loading duration under constant 2 kg load (up to 1 hour)
limitations_inferred: The linear Euler-Bernoulli beam model neglects complex non-linear contact mechanics, friction between particles, hyperelastic membrane deformation, and coupled torsion-bending observed experimentally.

Elevated operating temperatures (70 deg C for SMP, As = 60 deg C for SMA) could induce thermal fatigue or material degradation of the surrounding elastomer membrane and organic granular filler over repeated cycling.
Manual deformation restricts practical deployment in fully autonomous robotic systems without external assisting manipulators or actuators.
Passive cooling to ambient air limits cycle bandwidth and operational speed in tasks requiring rapid repeated softening and stiffening cycles.
Organic coffee grounds may be prone to moisture absorption, compaction, or degradation over time compared to engineered synthetic particles.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The prototype links could not return to their initial shape perfectly, retaining residual deformation after recovery.
The SMP sheet employed was thin, resulting in small shape recovery force.
The granular powder (coffee grounds) within the membrane was not optimized for the proposed link.
Coffee grounds were distributed non-uniformly inside the silicone rubber membrane, contributing to incomplete shape recovery in Prototype 2.
The prototypes were deformed manually during testing rather than via integrated robotic actuation.
Joule heating of shape memory materials is a relatively slow process that can slow down overall robotic operational speed.
Prototype 1 possesses orthotropic deformation resistance, potentially introducing unwanted waiting time if link axial rotation is required to reorient stiffness.
Prototype 2 lacked closed-loop temperature feedback control during SMA heating.
Gripping performance was assessed qualitatively without quantitative pull-off force measurements.
main_results: Demonstrated successful realization of four distinct stiffness levels by combining jamming pressure states and shape-memory material thermal states.

Prototype 1 achieved a maximum vertical bending stiffness change of approximately 33 times between unjammed state above Tg and jammed state below Tg, with jamming exerting a stronger stiffness effect than SMP thermal switching.

Prototype 1 exhibited significant orthotropic behavior: horizontal stiffness was greater than vertical stiffness, with horizontal loading producing non-linear response due to combined bending and twisting.

Unjammed stiffness below Tg for Prototype 1 (0.23 N/mm) was lower than beam calculation (0.56 N/mm) due to decoupled membrane deformation, while jammed stiffness difference across Tg (0.68 N/mm) closely matched theoretical prediction (0.56 N/mm).
Prototype 2 with SMA wires demonstrated substantially higher stiffness than Prototype 1, and its unjammed stiffness matched martensite beam model predictions (0.13 N/mm).
Both prototypes overcame the self-weight sag limitation of conventional unjammed granular manipulators, supporting their own weight horizontally when unjammed.
Prototype 2 recovered its shape in 0.24 times the duration required by Prototype 1, though both exhibited incomplete shape recovery.
Both prototypes held a 2 kg dead load stably for 1 hour with minimal deflection after initial loading, verifying robust shape fixity.
Cyclic loading (10 cycles) showed hysteresis and progressive reduction in reaction force across iterations for both prototypes.
Both prototypes successfully conformed to and gripped five distinct everyday objects without dropping.
modeling_methods: Euler-Bernoulli linear beam bending / cantilever deflection model: P/delta = 3*n*E*I / L^3
Linear regression approximation of force versus displacement curves below 20 N force to calculate bending stiffness (gradient)
performance_metrics: Tip deflection over time under 2 kg load (mm)
Shape recovery duration (s / min) and relative recovery speed ratio (0.24x)
Hysteresis and reaction force loss across 10 reciprocating cycles (N)
Self-weight retention capability in horizontal unjammed cantilever state
possible_gap_implications: Embedding shape-memory backbones within granular jamming envelopes directly resolves the self-weight sagging failure mode typical of unjammed granular continuum structures while adding multi-tier stiffness modulation.

However, the reliance on thermal phase transitions introduces inherent temporal delays and thermal dissipation challenges that must be overcome before hybrid variable-stiffness links can match the bandwidth of purely fluidic or motorized continuum mechanisms in dynamic environments.
paper.research_objective: To design, fabricate, and experimentally evaluate a variable-stiffness deformable link combining shape-memory materials (SMP or SMA) and granular jamming to achieve four stiffness states, shape fixity, self-weight support in the unjammed state, and shape recovery for robot arm and gripping applications.
paper.research_problem: Soft robots struggle to achieve high positioning accuracy and large load-bearing capacity, while conventional rigid motor-driven robots lack backdrivability and safety for human interaction; additionally, conventional granular jamming manipulators cannot support their own weight in a horizontal unjammed state, and shape memory materials suffer from slow Joule heating.
paper.title: Variable-Stiffness and Deformable Link Using Shape-Memory Material and Jamming Transition Phenomenon
